summary: Stale-state race on matchID change — no abort, no state reset; previous replay's data leaks into the new view.
failure_scenario: Navigate /replay/A → /replay/B before A's fetch resolves. (1) No reset: while B is loading, the page still renders A's title/players/charts because `a` is not cleared on dep change. (2) Race: if A's response arrives after B's (slow disk, server doing replay.Run for A), `setA(A)` overwrites the just-arrived B data; page now permanently shows A under URL /replay/B until another navigation.

summary: Committed dist HTML references hashed JS/CSS assets that are not git-tracked — fresh clone → blank page.
failure_scenario: Only `dist/index.html` is tracked (`git ls-files internal/replay/webui/dist` returns just that one file). The HTML hard-codes `/assets/index-D4V8UJqV.js` and `/assets/index-D8J_MQHF.css`. A fresh checkout + `go build ./cmd/replayreport` embeds only index.html via `//go:embed all:dist`; visiting / serves the HTML, but both asset URLs 404 → blank page with no React mounted. Worse: next web build emits different hashes, so the committed HTML drifts out of sync with the assets every rebuild.

summary: Phase markers iterate per player and draw duplicate lines + overlapping labels for every player who reached the same phase.
failure_scenario: In a 2-player game, both players have `phase_timings: {phase_town: 360}`. The outer loop pushes N identical shapes and N identical annotations to the same x,y. Plotly draws stacked text 'phase_town' on top of itself, and the dashed line is drawn twice (no opacity change). Same effect for `phase_city` etc.; in a 4v4 it's 8x duplication.

summary: Phase/engagement markers carry no player attribution — the chart can't tell you who phased up or who initiated combat.
failure_scenario: Annotation text is just the phase key ('phase_village') and engagement lines are uniformly red regardless of source player. Looking at the rendered chart you cannot distinguish 'I went City' from 'opponent went City', or 'my engagement at t=400' from 'their counter-attack at t=405'. Defeats the primary analytic value of the chart.

summary: Player attribution is dropped: `Object.values(...)` throws away the player ID before the row is built.
failure_scenario: Map iterates `Object.values(analysis.metrics.players)` (line 7) and the row contains no player. A panic_garrison anomaly for P1 and for P2 are rendered as visually identical rows; user cannot tell whose units panicked. The map's keys (P1/P2/...) are right there but discarded.

summary: Outcome hard-coded to player 1; wrong (or '—') for any replay where P1 isn't the perspective of interest.
failure_scenario: `if fs, ok := a.FinalState.Players[1]; ok { outcome = fs.Outcome }`. In AI-vs-AI replays, observer slots, or replays where the saving player is P2/P3, the list shows '—' or the wrong player's outcome. Sorting by 'timestamp desc' works but the per-row outcome column lies.

summary: listReplays runs full replay.Run() for every directory on every request — O(N) parse work per page load with no HTTP-layer cache.
failure_scenario: User refreshes the index page → for each of ~85 replay dirs, the handler re-invokes `replay.Run(dir)`. Even if the mtime cache short-circuits the heavy parse, the loop still reads metadata.json + stat + JSON-decode per dir per request. With 100+ replays, index page is visibly slow and CPU-spiky on repeated polling/refresh. Cache the list response in the handler (with mtime invalidation) instead.

summary: `var items []replayListItem` marshals as JSON `null` when no replays — violates the documented API contract `[]ReplayListItem`.
failure_scenario: Empty replay root → handler returns body `null`, not `[]`. The frontend already papers over this in api.ts:8 with `?? []` (and the commit message 8cd685e admits this), but any other consumer (curl scripts, future SPA pages, the api_test.go fixtures) sees the wrong type. CLAUDE.md REST contract explicitly promises an array. Initialize as `items := []replayListItem{}`.

summary: Duration shown as integer minutes only — truncates seconds and is inconsistent with IndexPage's mm:ss format.
failure_scenario: `Math.floor(a.game.duration_ms / 60000)` displays a 4:55 game as '4 мин', a 0:50 game as '0 мин'. Same data on the index card renders as '4:55'. Reuse `formatDuration` from IndexPage (or hoist to a shared util).

summary: Hardcoded white text on raw player color — unreadable on light backgrounds (yellow, white player slots).
failure_scenario: 0 A.D. assigns colors like Yellow `rgb(255,255,0)` and White `rgb(255,255,255)` to player slots. Chip renders 'PlayerName (athen)' in white on near-white background; the 1px text shadow barely helps. Compute relative luminance from `(r,g,b)` and pick black-or-white text accordingly.

summary: TypeScript `strict` mode is off — no strictNullChecks, no noImplicitAny, no strict function types.
failure_scenario: Only `noUnusedLocals/Parameters/erasableSyntaxOnly/noFallthroughCasesInSwitch` are enabled; `strict` is absent. Real consequences in this codebase: `data` accesses like `(e.data as { template?: string })` would otherwise be required; `analysis.metrics.players` being `undefined` would be flagged; the `any` cast on Plotly would still need the explicit `unknown` escape but the rest of the code loses null-safety. Add `

summary: Ships the full ~3 MB `plotly.js-dist-min` bundle for a single stacked-bar chart — order-of-magnitude bigger than needed.
failure_scenario: `import * as PlotlyMod from 'plotly.js-dist-min'` pulls every trace type (scatter3d, mesh3d, geo, gl3d, mapbox, sankey, etc.). The chart only uses 'bar' + shapes/annotations. Use `plotly.js-basic-dist-min` (~1 MB) or build a custom bundle with just the bar trace. SPA initial load shrinks dramatically.

summary: Three dead Plotly dependencies still declared after the 2064c62 migration to direct Plotly.newPlot.
failure_scenario: `plotly.js`, `react-plotly.js`, `@types/react-plotly.js` are all in `dependencies`/`devDependencies` but not imported anywhere (grep finds zero refs). `plotly.js` alone duplicates the bundle already pulled by `plotly.js-dist-min` in node_modules, doubling install size and lockfile churn. Remove all three.

summary: Entire 185-line Vite-scaffold CSS file (counter/hero/next-steps) is unreferenced; same for /src/assets/{react,vite}.svg and hero.png.
failure_scenario: `grep -rn 'App.css\|react.svg\|vite.svg\|hero.png' web/src web/index.html` returns nothing. App.css is never imported (App.tsx imports nothing CSS; main.tsx imports only index.css). The CSS targets selectors that don't exist (#center, #next-steps, .hero, .counter). Just delete the file and the three image assets — pure scaffold residue.

summary: SPA fallback does an `fs.Stat` and (when falling through) an `fs.ReadFile('index.html')` on every non-API request.
failure_scenario: Each request to `/`, `/replay/...`, or any static asset re-walks the embedded FS metadata, and the fallback path re-reads the entire index.html bytes from the embed for every miss. Pre-load `index.html` into a `[]byte` at server construction and serve via `bytes.NewReader` + `http.ServeContent`. Same goes for caching the `dist` sub-FS handler. Negligible per-request, but a needless hot-path allocation.
